english_verification.review_scope: Checked specific proper names against the original main-card text_en glossary and Mod localization, plus representative historical, mission, and national-idea claims; this is not a full source-code audit.
unresolved: The Chinese-source research summary says the 1452 Bulwari rebellion defeated Tluukt and that Jaddar's legions eventually annexed her in later history. The retrieved English wiki passage instead says she retained her gnollish subordinates and the Šad Sur after the defeat and does not substantiate later annexation. The article preserves the attributed Chinese-source summary and records this discrepancy without an independent historical ruling.
The Mod records Tluukt's accession in 1413; the retrieved wiki dates the beginning of her aggressive rise to the 1420s. These source claims are retained separately, with no reconciled chronology.

The wiki chunks do not verify every mission mechanic or each national-idea effect. The card values remain faithful translations of the source fields; the code-to-display mapping of reduced_liberty_desire_on_same_continent = 15 versus the source display of +1500% remains unreconciled.

Community play-experience statements in the source article were not independently checked in this scoped source pass; the 1507 siege remains national-idea narrative rather than a claim verified by the three retrieved wiki chunks.

rationale.campaign_length: 84 missions directly defined for F28, including conditional branches; the entire tree cannot be completed in a single run.
rationale.colonization: No clearly defined colonization-focused main arc.
rationale.complexity: Branches, the leader’s limited lifespan, and subject loyalty interact.
rationale.dark_story: Enslavement, rule by terror, and intrigue run throughout.
rationale.difficulty: Requires good timing; not quantified through hands-on testing.
rationale.diplomacy: Alliances, betrayal, tribute, and subjects remain important throughout.
rationale.early_pressure: A major early war and the leader’s lifespan create intense pressure.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Tluukt’s powerful Evocation magic and Xhazobine rituals shape the opening.
rationale.narrative_density: The leader’s death, branching conflicts, and later legacy form a complete character arc.
rationale.tall_play: Mines and urban reforms serve the pursuit of hegemony.
rationale.trade_economy: Trade ports, markets, mining, and an economy based on enslavement all feature.
rationale.warfare: The conquest of Bulwar and the conflict involving Zokka and Jaddar are central.

identity.formation_scope: No formation is required; the native F28 mission tree includes outcome branches involving Zokka and Jaddar.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; excludes optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses. Multiple candidate sets and conditional outcomes are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneous. Whether a formed country adopts new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
Gnolls share a long history with Bulwar. In 984 BA gnolls have invaded Bulwar for the first time, establishing several kingdoms there with the greatest of all being the All-High Kingdom of Zehia, centered around Sur mountains. Zehia's core land occupied roughly the same territory Tluukt holds in 1444, and many of our gnolls are direct descendants of the first invaders. The gnollish rule over Bulwar continued to wax and wane through centuries, until eventually being ended by the elves under Jaher. Defeated by Jaherian legions, gnolls ended up pushed into the hills and deserts on the outskirts of Bulwar with almost no city centres under direct control.

And yet, we remain and remember. We remember the glory of the past, we remember the successes of the Xhazobines, we remember the Age of Monsters. We do remember it all... but Bulwari humans seem to be forgetting, and the time has come for gnolls to remind them.

description.text:
Tluukt is a conglomeration of several disparate tribes of southern Bulwar, united in early 1400s by Tluukt, a powerful gnollish mage. Tluukt is saddened by the state in which gnolls of Bulwar are found today and she believes that the gnollish society should be reformed.

She wishes to restore the gnollish rule to Bulwar by modernising the structure of gnollish packs and ensuring both internal stability and total loyalty and support of subjects. Having already done so inside her pack, Tluukt now looks north towards Bulwar proper. The Cleaver of Realms shall make a new grand gnollish state, and none may stand in her way.

description.text: The fall of Zokka came to Tluukt as a shock at first. A powerful ally, he was slain in a single combat with the pack utterly collapsing. But then, Tluukt saw an opportunity. Thousands of gnollish soldiers willingly joined our pack, filled with zealous rage and fury against Jaddar and his elven kind. The Devourer of the Sun might have fell, but the sun has not seen the last of gnolls just yet.

description.text:
Our human subjects tend to get scared easily by our gnollish nature. While we are not directly opposed to it - it is nice knowing they fear their rulers - this eventually can get very tiresome and annoying, especially when trying to deal with them.

Luckily, not all humans are like that and there are those that are able to listen to orders and execute them. Using them as our intermediates we can hold an indirect control over humans. Tight enough to hold them under control, loose enough to let them do their work.

description.text: While gnolls are primarily known as scavengers, we are also good at hiding supplies that might be needed later. When Jaher and his legions invaded Bulwar and ended gnollish rule, countless of hidden weapons, maps and pieces of armour were lost in the sands. Luckily for us, neither humans not elves were able to find those caches, allowing Tluukt armies to finally utilise them centuries later.

description.text: Slavery is a large part of gnollish society, and our loss of control over Bulwar severely limited and practically ended the practice of slavery in the region. This changed when our Pack Mistress has managed to enfold the humans' into the pack's domain following invasion of Bulwar proper, bringing a large amount of potential slaves to the market. Citizens of humans were left in shock after our slavemasters started rounding up random humans, putting them in chains and sending south to Tluukt's palace. Let Bulwari slavery be reignited in defiance of wannabe gods and their blind followers!

description.text:
Following the death of its founder, Tluukt faced defeat after defeat against elves and Bulwari humans alike, until eventually the gnolls were surrounded in Grixekyr. The pack continued to exist in such a state for the next few decades, continually fortifying their lands and deterring increasingly rare Bulwari attacks. Alas, all good things must come to an end.

In 1507 Tluukt's old enemies, the Jaddari, declared the final war against the gnolls in Bulwar. While some traitorous gnolls sided with the elves and accepted the Jadd, the loyal gnolls of Tluukt fought to the last soldier, but despite their ferocity were pushed back all the way into the recently restored Ekluzagnu. Here, the Jaddari led an extremely long and costly siege, fighting floor by floor to kill every single gnoll in the fortress. Ironically, the very same place destroyed by Xhazobine ended up being the site of last stand of gnollish rule in Bulwar.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who dislike opening races against time or enslavement themes.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Use the leader’s magic to break through early, expand along the conflict branches, then rule Bulwar through subjects and reforms.
player_overview.overview: Begin in 1444 as a gnoll pack in Šad Sur. Tluukt excels at Evocation magic and intrigue; the mission tree branches according to the wars involving Zokka and Jaddar. Conquer the valley, manipulate subjects, reshape pack rule, and try to accomplish great things before the matriarch dies. This is a dark conquest story steeped in enslavement and rule by fear.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy high-pressure conquest, powerful mages, complex subject management, and villain-centered stories.
signature_features: 84 conditional missions; race to accomplish them while the leader lives.
Political branches involving Zokka and Jaddar.
A subject network, magical warfare, and the creation of a gnoll empire.
player_overview.tagline: A powerful witch-matriarch leads the gnolls in a bid for Bulwar; what she accomplishes before her death determines how the empire remembers her.

reasons: A strongly character-centered story about a gnoll witch.
The outcome of the war changes the mission path.
Subject governance transforms a pack into an empire.
warnings: Tluukt’s death changes the structure of rewards.
The early branches and major-war pacing are demanding.
Enslavement is a prominent part of the narrative.

positive_indicators: Some urban governance and military-political reforms improve life for the packs.
values.rationale: The missions explicitly enslave and sell Bulwari inhabitants and harpies, replenish the workforce after enslaved miners die, and treat subjects’ free will as something that may be taken away. Governance yields some public benefit through infrastructure, but its core treats sapient beings as resources.
red_flags: Mine operations continue to expand despite mass deaths among enslaved miners.
Subjects’ free will is institutionally denied.
